ai.definition: Mars exploration involves the systematic investigation of the planet Mars using spacecraft, rovers, satellites, and other technological means to understand its geology, atmosphere, climate, and potential for supporting human life.
ai.howItWorks: Exploration is conducted through a combination of remote sensing from orbiters and landers, surface analysis by rovers, and sample return missions. Data collected helps in understanding Mars' past habitability and future potential as a colony site.
ai.problemSolved: Identifying resources, assessing environmental conditions, and determining the feasibility of human settlement on Mars.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing specialized spacecraft components, electronics, and robotic systems capable of withstanding harsh Martian environments. Materials must be robust against radiation, extreme temperatures, and dust storms.
ai.buildProcess: Components are designed using advanced CAD software, then manufactured in clean rooms under strict quality control to ensure reliability in space conditions. Testing includes thermal cycling, vibration testing, and exposure to simulated Mars atmospheres.
ai.costDrivers: High development costs, specialized materials, and the need for long-term sustainability of missions contribute significantly to overall expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to grow as private companies and space agencies invest more in infrastructure and technology readiness for human Mars missions.
ai.regulation: Governed by international agreements such as the Outer Space Treaty, with additional regulations from individual countries regarding their space programs. Ethical considerations around resource extraction and environmental impact are also key.
ai.risks: Technological challenges, financial constraints, geopolitical tensions, and ethical concerns about resource exploitation and planetary protection pose significant risks.
ai.profitability: Potential for long-term economic benefits through resource utilization and tourism, but current projects are primarily driven by scientific exploration and technological advancement rather than direct profitability.
ai.futureDevelopment: Focus on reducing mission costs, improving rover autonomy, developing in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) technologies, and expanding international cooperation in space exploration.

glossary.def: The process of extracting and using local resources on Mars, such as water ice or minerals, to support human exploration.

subsystems.name: Launch and cruise stage
subsystems.role: gets the spacecraft off Earth and steers it across interplanetary space.

subsystems.name: Entry, descent and landing system
subsystems.role: slows a vehicle arriving at about 20,000 km/h to a soft touchdown in a thin atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: keeps instruments alive through Martian nights of around −90 °C.
parts: radioisotope thermoelectric generator or solar arrays

subsystems.name: Mobility and sample handling
subsystems.role: lets the robot reach interesting rocks and take pieces of them.

subsystems.name: Science instruments
subsystems.role: identify minerals, chemistry and ancient environments.

subsystems.name: Communications and operations
subsystems.role: relays commands up and data down, and turns the data into the next day's plan.

buildSteps.title: Set the science question
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the mission must answer — past habitability, present-day life, or resource mapping — and pick a landing site that can answer it.

buildSteps.title: Design and build the flight system
buildSteps.detail: Rover chassis, instruments, aeroshell and parachute are fabricated and then shaken, baked and frozen in thermal-vacuum chambers that mimic Mars.

buildSteps.title: Launch in a transfer window
buildSteps.detail: Earth and Mars line up roughly every 26 months, so the launch date is fixed years in advance and the whole spacecraft must be ready for it.

buildSteps.title: Cruise for about seven months
buildSteps.detail: The craft coasts 55–400 million km, firing thrusters occasionally to fine-tune its aim at a target ellipse a few kilometres wide.

buildSteps.title: Land
buildSteps.detail: The heat shield absorbs the entry, a parachute deploys at supersonic speed, and retro-rockets or a sky crane lower the rover to the surface — the phase engineers call the seven minutes of terror.

buildSteps.title: Commission and drive
buildSteps.detail: The rover unfolds, checks every instrument, then begins driving across terrain it must judge for itself, because a radio round trip takes 5–20 minutes each way.

buildSteps.title: Drill, cache and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Rock cores are powdered and examined onboard; some are sealed in tubes and left on the surface for a future mission to collect.

buildSteps.title: Relay and plan each sol
buildSteps.detail: Data goes up through orbiting relay spacecraft to Earth antennas overnight, and the team writes the next Martian day's commands.

buildSteps.title: For crews: make the return trip possible
buildSteps.detail: A crewed mission would need a Mars ascent vehicle, propellant and oxygen made from the atmosphere, and a habitat shielded from radiation — none of which exists yet.

prerequisites.why: everything starts with throwing a multi-tonne payload onto a Mars trajectory.
large Earth antennas and orbiting relays are the only way to command and retrieve data.
signals take minutes to arrive, so the vehicle must avoid hazards without a human in the loop.
they survive dust storms and winter, but plutonium-238 supply is small and slow to make.

prerequisites.tech: In-situ resource use at useful scale
prerequisites.why: a small instrument on Perseverance made oxygen from carbon dioxide, but no mission has produced propellant quantities.

prerequisites.tech: Crewed life support, radiation shielding and Mars ascent
prerequisites.why: without a way to keep people alive and lift them off Mars, exploration stays robotic.

pathway.milestone: robotic rovers, landers and orbiters characterising ancient habitable environments
pathway.unlocks: the geological and climate knowledge any later mission depends on.

pathway.milestone: Mars Sample Return: bringing the cached tubes back to Earth laboratories
pathway.unlocks: dating and life-detection techniques far beyond anything a rover can carry.

pathway.milestone: robotic demonstration of propellant and oxygen production from the Martian atmosphere
pathway.unlocks: a way to refuel on Mars instead of hauling return fuel from Earth.

pathway.milestone: crewed surface missions and a sustained outpost
pathway.unlocks: field geology by humans and the first steps toward permanent presence.
